line: The alchemical opus in Jung's texts (CW9ii, CW11, CW12, CW14, CW16): the four colours, the operations, the matter and the elements.

opus.line: The four stages by their colours: blackening, whitening, yellowing, reddening (CW12 ¶333).

stages.name: Nigredo
stages.line: The blackening: the initial state, present in the prima materia from the beginning or produced by the separation of the elements (CW12 ¶334).

quotes.text: The raven is a nigredo symbol.—Jamsthaler, Viatorium spagyricum (1625) The nigredo or blackness (fig. 115) is the initial state, either present from the beginning as a quality of the prima materia, the chaos or massa confusa, or else produced by the separation (solutio, separatio, divisio, putrefactio) of the elements.
The nigredo signifies the mortificatio, putrefactio, solutio, separatio, divisio, etc., a state of dissolution and decomposition that precedes the synthesis.
The opus is far from having come to an end at this point, for the nigredo (terra nigra) still prevails and the substance of the stone is still black.

psyche.line: Jung writes that the nigredo corresponds to the encounter with the shadow (CW12 ¶41) and to the darkness of the unconscious (CW14 ¶646).

quotes.text: The author of this sentence must have been undergoing the experience of the nigredo, the first stage of the work, which was felt as “melancholia” in alchemy and corresponds to the encounter with the shadow in psychology.
The nigredo corresponds to the darkness of the unconscious, which contains in the first place the inferior personality, the shadow.
In the nigredo, the “dark night of the soul,” the psychic contents free themselves from their attachment to the body, and the nature and meaning of this connection are recognized.

stages.name: Albedo
stages.line: The whitening: the silver or moon condition, which still has to be raised to the sun condition (CW12 ¶334).

quotes.text: It is the silver or moon condition, which still has to be raised to the sun condition.
The albedo is, so to speak, the daybreak, but not till the rubedo is it sunrise.
“3 The whitening (albedo or dealbatio) is likened to the ortus solis, the sunrise; it is the light, the illumination, that follows the darkness.

psyche.line: Jung writes that from the darkness of the unconscious comes the light of illumination, the albedo (CW14 ¶220), and that the role of Luna devolves upon the anima (CW14 ¶218).

quotes.text: From the darkness of the unconscious comes the light of illumination, the albedo.
This role of Luna devolves upon the anima, as she personifies the plurality of archetypes

stages.name: Citrinitas
stages.line: The yellowing, xanthosis or citrinitas: the third of the four stages (CW12 ¶333); the transition to the rubedo (CW12 ¶334).

quotes.text: Later, about the fifteenth or sixteenth century, the colours were reduced to three, and the xanthosis, otherwise called the citrinitas, gradually fell into disuse or was but seldom mentioned.
The transition to the rubedo is formed by the citrinitas, though this, as we have said, was omitted later.
the ash-colour, the whitening, and the yellowing are over, you will see the Philosophical Stone
Corresponding to the xanthesis, citrinitas, or yellowing.

psyche.line: Jung writes that the four colours in the dream represent the transition from trinity to quaternity (CW12 ¶220).

quotes.text: The fact is that the four colours in the dream represent the transition from trinity to quaternity and thus to the squared circle (figs. 59, 60), which, according to the alchemists, comes nearest to the lapis on account of its roundness or perfect simplicity.

stages.name: Rubedo
stages.line: The reddening: the marriage of the red man and the white woman, Sol and Luna (CW14 ¶307); the second and usually final stage (CW14 ¶434).

quotes.text: The alchemists termed this the rubedo, in which the marriage of the red man and the white woman, Sol and Luna, is consummated.
Luna in herself is spirit, and she at once joins her husband Sol, thus initiating the second and usually final stage, the rubedo.
The red and the white are King and Queen, who may also celebrate their “chymical wedding” at this stage (fig. 116).
The rubedo then follows direct from the albedo as the result of raising the heat of the fire to its highest intensity.

psyche.line: Jung writes that the growing redness denotes an increase of warmth and light coming from the sun, consciousness (CW14 ¶307).

quotes.text: The growing redness (rubedo) which now follows denotes an increase of warmth and light coming from the sun, consciousness.
This third stage of the coniunctio was depicted51 after the manner of an Assumption and Coronation of Mary, in which the Mother of God represents the body.

bridge.line: The peacock's tail (cauda pavonis): the many colours lead to the one white colour that contains all colours (CW12 ¶334); the albedo follows it immediately (CW14 ¶434).

quotes.text: From this the washing (ablutio, baptisma) either leads direct to the whitening (albedo), or else the soul (anima) released at the “death” is reunited with the dead body and brings about its resurrection, or again the “many colours” (omnes colores), or “peacock’s tail” (cauda pavonis), lead to the one white colour that contains all colours.

At this moment something in the nature of a miracle occurs: the material solution loses its earthy heaviness, and solvent and solute together pass into a higher state immediately following the cauda pavonis, namely the albedo.

operations.name: Calcinatio
operations.line: Calcinatio is named among the kinds of burning by which the spirit is expelled; the end-product is called ash (CW14 ¶247).

quotes.text: As the expulsion of the spirit was effected by various kinds of burning (combustio, adustio, calcinatio, assatio, sublimatio, incineratio, etc.), it was natural to call the end-product “ash”—again in a double sense as scoria, faex, etc., and as the spirit or bird of Hermes.
In other words, the ash is the spirit that dwells in the glorified body.

Without fire and salt the heathen would not have been able to offer sacrifice, and the evangelist Mark had said that “every one shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt.” h. The Interpretation and Meaning of Salt Salt as much as ash is a synonym for the albedo (or dealbatio), and is identical with “the white stone, the white sun, the full moon, the fruitful white earth, cleansed and calcined.”

operations.name: Solutio
operations.line: The philosophical water is the stone or the prima materia itself and also its solvent (CW12 ¶337); solvent and solute pass into a higher state (CW14 ¶434).

quotes.text: During the solutio, separatio, and extractio the succus lunariae (juice of the moon-plant), blood, or aqua permanens is either applied or extracted.
For it is the picture of the first dissolution and coagulation and of the resultant second dissolution.

At this moment something in the nature of a miracle occurs: the material solution loses its earthy heaviness, and solvent and solute together pass into a higher state immediately following the cauda pavonis, namely the albedo.
the philosophical water is the stone or the prima materia itself; but at the same time, it is also its solvent

operations.name: Coagulatio
operations.line: The coagulating sulphur, turned outwards in the corporal gold, is turned inwards (CW14 ¶134); the peacock's tail appears in the coagulation (CW12 ¶400).

quotes.text: When the gold (Sol) and his bride (Luna) are united, “the coagulating sulphur, which in the corporal gold was turned outwards [extroversion], is turned inwards” (i.e., introverted).75
A third capacity is that of coagulating, and a fourth and fifth those of tincturing (tingere, colorare) and maturing (maturare).
This leads to the true eclipse of the sun and one should put a rainbow on either side to suggest the peacock’s tail that then appears in the coagulation.

operations.name: Sublimatio
operations.line: A shining white soul flies up to heaven with the spirit; its fixation takes place when the secret stone is added (CW12 ¶462).

quotes.text: At the end of the sublimation [fig. 200] there germinates, through the mediation of the spirit, a shining white soul [anima candida] which flies up to heaven with the spirit [cf. fig. 134].

But as regards the fixation and permanence of the soul and spirit at the end of the sublimation, this takes place when the secret stone is added, which cannot be grasped by the senses, but only by the intellect, through inspiration or divine revelation, or through the teaching of an initiate.
For the same reason the process of sublimation is known in Arabic alchemy as the “great south wind,” referring to the heating of the retort.

operations.name: Mortificatio
operations.line: The slaying of the dragon, the mortificatio of the first, dangerous, poisonous stage of the anima (CW14 ¶168); a mutilation performed on the lion (CW14 ¶169).

quotes.text: “Unless ye slay me” usually refers to the slaying of the dragon, the mortificatio of the first, dangerous, poisonous stage of the anima (= Mercurius), freed from her imprisonment in the prima materia.
The mortificatio, this time only in the form of a mutilation, is also performed on the lion, whose paws are cut off, and on the bird, whose wings are clipped.
It signifies the overcoming of the old and obsolete as well as of the dangerous preliminary stages which are characterized by animal-symbols.

operations.name: Separatio
operations.line: The earth is separated from the primal water, and the composite natures are changed back into their initial elements (CW12 ¶367).

quotes.text: The painful conflict that begins with the nigredo or tenebrositas is described by the alchemists as the separatio or divisio elementorum, the solutio, calcinatio, incineratio, or as dismemberment of the body, excruciating animal sacrifices, amputation of the mother’s hands or the lion’s paws, atomization of the bridegroom in the body of the bride, and so on.

The second horizontal series represents a higher stage in the process: in column I, the composite natures are decomposed or changed back into their initial elements; in column II, the earth is separated from the (primal) water as in the Book of Genesis, a favourite theme in alchemy; in column III, there is a separation into categories; and column IV is concerned with the psychological act of discrimination.

The second horizontal series represents a higher stage in the process: in column I, the composite natures are decomposed or changed back into their initial elements; in column II, the earth is separated from the (primal) water as in the Book of Genesis, a favourite theme in alchemy; in column III, there is a separation into categories; and column IV is concerned with the psychological act of discrimination.

operations.name: Coniunctio
operations.line: Jung writes that when the opposites unite, all energy ceases: there is no more flow (CW16 ¶467).

quotes.text: Just as Gabricus dies after becoming united with his sister, and the sonlover always comes to an early end after consummating the hierosgamos with the mother-goddess of the Near East, so, after the coniunctio oppositorum, deathlike stillness reigns.
When the opposites unite, all energy ceases: there is no more flow.

operations.name: Distillatio
operations.line: The production of one from four by distillation and sublimation in circular form, so that the soul or spirit is extracted in its purest state (CW12 ¶165).

quotes.text: The production of one from four is the result of a process of distillation and sublimation which takes the so-called “circular” form: the distillate is subjected to sundry distillations35 so that the “soul” or “spirit” shall be extracted in its purest state.

The production of one from four is the result of a process of distillation and sublimation which takes the so-called “circular” form: the distillate is subjected to sundry distillations35 so that the “soul” or “spirit” shall be extracted in its purest state.
Soul and spirit must be separated from the body, and this is equivalent to death: “Therefore Paul of Tarsus saith, Cupio dissolvi, et esse cum Christo.

operations.name: Circulatio
operations.line: The wheel is a favourite symbol for the circulatio, meaning the ascensus and descensus (CW12 ¶214); the rotation motif is dynamic, not static (CW12 ¶283).

quotes.text: It is to be noted that the wheel is a favourite symbol in alchemy for the circulating process, the circulatio.

By this is meant firstly the ascensus and descensus, for instance the ascending and descending birds symbolizing the precipitation of vapours, and secondly the rotation of the universe as a model for the work, and hence the cycling of the year in which the work takes place.
The rotation motif indicates that the symbol of the circle is to be thought of not as static but as dynamic.

Michael Maier actually takes the opus circulatorium as an image of the sun’s course: For while the hero, like a joyful giant, rises in the east and hastens to his sinking in the west, that he may forever return out of the east, he sets in motion these circulations, depositing in the shining substance of the quicksilver, as in a mirror, forms [wherein] by human diligence the gold may be sought, cleansed from impurities, tested by fire and water, and put to a use pleasing to God the Creator.

operations.name: Putrefactio
operations.line: Jung writes that the transformation is effected by putrefaction, which is synonymous with the nigredo, the grave, and death (CW14 ¶714).

quotes.text: Then, it causes or signifies the putrefactio, “which in our day was never seen,” says the Rosarium
As the legend tells us, the picture represents the putrefactio, the corruption, the decay of a once living creature.
The transformation is effected by putrefaction, which is synonymous with the nigredo, the grave, and death.

matter.name: The prima materia
matter.line: Jung lists many names the alchemists gave the prima materia (CW12 ¶425); it sometimes coincides with the nigredo (CW12 ¶433).

quotes.text: For one alchemist the prima materia was quicksilver, for others it was ore, iron, gold, lead, salt, sulphur, vinegar, water, air, fire, earth, blood, water of life, lapis, poison, spirit, cloud, sky, dew, shadow, sea, mother, moon, dragon, Venus, chaos, microcosm (fig. 162).
That is why the prima materia sometimes coincides with the idea of the initial stage of the process, the nigredo.
In alchemy the egg stands for the chaos apprehended by the artifex, the prima materia containing the captive world-soul.

matter.name: The vessel
matter.line: The Hermetic vessel is a matrix or uterus from which the filius philosophorum, the stone, is born; Jung calls it a true symbol (CW12 ¶338).

quotes.text: Another, no less important, idea is that of the Hermetic vessel (vas Hermetis), typified by the retorts or melting-furnaces that contained the substances to be transformed (fig. 119).
It is a kind of matrix or uterus from which the filius philosophorum, the miraculous stone, is to be born18 (fig. 120).
since the vessel is more a mystical idea, a true symbol
The vas bene clausum (well-sealed vessel) is a precautionary measure very frequently mentioned in alchemy, and is the equivalent of the magic circle.

matter.name: Mercurius
matter.line: Mercurius comes lowest as prima materia and highest as lapis philosophorum (CW12 ¶84); the alchemist means quicksilver and inwardly the world-creating spirit concealed in matter (CW12 ¶404).

quotes.text: In the alchemical hierarchy of gods Mercurius comes lowest as prima materia and highest as lapis philosophorum.

It then transpired that Hermes or Mercurius possessed a double nature, being a chthonic god of revelation and also the spirit of quicksilver, for which reason he was represented as a hermaphrodite (fig. 22).
When the alchemist speaks of Mercurius, on the face of it he means quicksilver, but inwardly he means the world-creating spirit concealed or imprisoned in matter.

matter.name: Sulphur and salt
matter.line: Sulphur as prima materia is burning and corrosive (CW14 ¶134); salt is a cosmic principle correlated with the feminine, lunar side (CW14 ¶240); Mercurius partakes of the red sulphur and the lunar salt (CW14 ¶235).

quotes.text: But its duplicity also has another meaning: on the one hand it is the prima materia, and in this form it is burning and corrosive (adurens), and “hostile” to the matter of the stone; on the other hand, when “cleansed of all impurities, it is the matter of our stone.”
In philosophical alchemy, salt is a cosmic principle. According to its position in the quaternity, it is correlated with the feminine, lunar side and with the upper, light half.
A subtle feature of the Sulphur-Mercurius-Sal formula is that the central figure, Mercurius, is by nature androgynous and thus partakes both of the masculine red sulphur and of the lunar salt.

matter.name: Metals and planets
matter.line: Jung writes that the seven allude to the seven planets and hence to the metals (CW12 ¶410); Maier writes that gold is the sun's image in the earth (CW12 ¶445).

quotes.text: The seven are an obvious allusion to the seven planets and hence to the metals (figs. 154, 155; cf. figs. 21, 79) which in the alchemical view spring from the hermaphrodite Mercurius.

In Chapter IX, “The Heavens,” we read: You shall take seven pieces of metal, of each and every metal as they are named after the planets, and shall stamp on each the character of the planet in the house of the same planet, and every piece shall be as large and thick as a rose noble.
The sun is the image of God, the heart62 is the sun’s image in man, just as gold is the sun’s image in the earth (also called Deus terrenus), and God is known in the gold.

matter.name: The stone
matter.line: The lapis philosophorum is often the prima materia, or the means of producing the gold (CW12 ¶335); Jung writes that the self, as totality, is a veritable lapis invisibilitatis (CW12 ¶247).

quotes.text: The lapis philosophorum, for instance, is often the prima materia, or the means of producing the gold; or again it is an altogether mystical being that is sometimes called Deus terrestris, Salvator, or filius macrocosmi, a figure we can only compare with the Gnostic Anthropos, the divine original man6 (fig. 117).
sometimes the philosophers’ stone, which, as hermaphrodite, contains both

But then it becomes clear that the animal is only leading up to the four colours (cf. dream 23, par. 212), which in their turn lead to the lapis, i.e., the diamond whose prism contains all the hues of the rainbow.
I may define “self” as the totality of the conscious and unconscious psyche, but this totality transcends our vision; it is a veritable lapis invisibilitatis.

elements.line: The four elements and the quinta essentia: CW12 ¶31, CW9ii ¶375 and ¶376, CW11 ¶104, and von Franz, Number and Time, p77.

quotes.text: There are always four elements, but often three of them are grouped together, with the fourth in a special position—sometimes earth, sometimes fire.

In the chaos the elements are not united, they are merely coexistent and have to be combined through the alchemical procedure. They are even hostile to one another and will not unite of their own accord.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

quotes.text: As already mentioned, the constitution of the lapis rests on the union of the four elements, which in their turn represent an unfolding of the unknowable inchoate state, or chaos.

cite.workTitle: Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self

quotes.text: Dorn breaks with the whole alchemical tradition inasmuch as he adopts the rigidly Christian standpoint that Three is One but Four is not, because Four attains to unity in the quinta essentia.

cite.workTitle: Psychology and Religion: West and East

quotes.text: The latter is not merely a fifth element added on to the four known ones, but represents their realized unity of existence.
